frame.caption: Cell — a preset, or "custom" with its diameter and length below
frame.name: CELL

frame.caption: Diameter (mm) — the cell's body; 0 takes the preset's
frame.name: CELL_D

frame.caption: Length (mm) — the cell's body, end face to end face; 0 takes the preset's
frame.name: CELL_L

frame.caption: Fit offset (mm) — added to the cell's diameter where the grip is drawn: positive if your coupons were tight, negative if loose
frame.name: FIT_OFFSET

frame.caption: Gap between cells (mm) — between neighbouring cells' bodies; at 0.8 the printed holes round neighbouring cells just meet
frame.name: CELL_GAP

frame.caption: Pitch (mm) — centre to centre, overriding diameter + gap: set it when your busbars or nickel strip fix it; 0 to leave it
frame.name: PITCH

frame.caption: Cell columns — cells across the block
frame.name: CELL_COLUMNS

frame.caption: Cell rows — cells deep
frame.name: CELL_ROWS

frame.caption: Printer size (mm) — the build volume's smallest side, which every side of the part must fit: 270 for a Snapmaker U1
frame.name: PRINTER_SIZE

frame.caption: Waves per cell — along the wall: 1 puts a crest at each cell's middle and a vent by each gap between cells
frame.name: WAVES_PER_CELL

frame.caption: Along share — the along-the-wall wave's share of the depth: 0.5 round vents; toward 0.7 tall slots; under 0.35 thin columns
frame.name: ALONG_SHARE

frame.caption: Wave spacing (mm) — how far apart the waves up the frame stand, rounded to fit: shorter, more and smaller vents
frame.name: UP_WAVELENGTH

frame.caption: Wave phase (degrees) — where the waves up the frame fall: 90 sets the contact lines evenly between the bands, 0 the vents
frame.name: UP_PHASE

frame.caption: Stagger — each cell's shift of the waves up the frame, in waves: 0.5 staggers the vents like brick; 0 lines them up in rows
frame.name: STAGGER

frame.caption: Trough depth (mm) — how far the wall stands off the cells between contacts: deeper, bigger vents and air channels
frame.name: TROUGH_DEPTH

frame.caption: Crest press (mm) — how far the crests reach past the cells' land, on radius; the land trims them, leaving the contact patches
frame.name: CREST_PRESS

frame.caption: Mirror — how far the outside follows the inside's wave, 0 to 1: 1 fully, opening the most; less, a thicker wall, smaller vents
frame.name: MIRROR

frame.caption: Grip — where the edge cells' bow springs sit: auto takes the gap between edge cells where a bow fits, else the wall
frame.name: GRIP

frame.caption: Bow span (mm) — a bow spring's span between its roots: 8 is tested, and the longest drawn
frame.name: BOW_SPAN

frame.caption: Shortest bow span (mm) — the shortest allowed: shorter, it is too stiff to spring. Untested below 8
frame.name: BOW_SPAN_MIN

frame.caption: Bow thickness (mm) — two lines of a 0.4 mm nozzle
frame.name: BOW_T

frame.caption: Bow press (mm) — how far the bows' faces stand inside the cell at their middle, on diameter: more grips harder
frame.name: BOW_PRESS

frame.caption: Bore clearance (mm) — the hole round the bows, past the cell, on diameter: a plain hole this size is a bit loose
frame.name: BORE_CLR

frame.caption: Thinnest neck (mm) — the narrowest plastic between two neighbouring pockets: four lines
frame.name: NECK_MIN

frame.caption: Arm tip width (mm) — where an arm between two cells is cut: thinner won't print as a wall
frame.name: ARM_TIP_W

frame.caption: Frame land clearance (mm) — the frame round each cell, on diameter: a block of cells slides in without binding
frame.name: FRAME_LAND_CLR

frame.caption: Shortest tie (mm) — the solid across the wall between two vents one above the other; columns are never narrower either
frame.name: TIE_MIN

frame.caption: Narrowest column (share) — the solid between two vents side by side, as a share of the along-the-wall wavelength
frame.name: COLUMN_MIN_SHARE

frame.caption: Least open (share) — the share of the wall between the bands that must open: less, and the vents are slivers
frame.name: OPEN_SHARE_MIN

frame.caption: Widest vent top (mm) — a vent's width 1 mm below its top, which the printer has to bridge: keep it to what yours bridges cleanly
frame.name: BRIDGE_MAX

frame.caption: Wall thickness (mm) — in the bands of bows: eight lines
frame.name: WALL_T

frame.caption: Bump depth (mm) — the bumps on the outside behind each cell, where the wall is otherwise plain
frame.name: BUMP_DEPTH

frame.caption: Band height (mm) — each band of bows near the ends: short, to leave more of the frame to the vents
frame.name: BAND_H

frame.caption: End clearance (mm) — the frame stops this far short of each end of the cells, clear of terminals and busbars
frame.name: END_CLR
